## Fixed: Live crashing on converted sets with instruments

Some converted sets still made Live crash right after opening them, even with 0.3.2. The real cause: when an instrument's settings couldn't be carried over to its VST3 (Spire, Omnisphere and other plug-ins whose VST3 isn't declared as a replacement), the old instrument was kept next to the new one **in the same chain**. A chain can only hold one instrument, and Live crashes loading a set that has two. (0.3.2's change matched Live's own file layout and stays in, but it wasn't what caused the crash.)

## New: the track is duplicated instead

For such an instrument, the converter now duplicates its track:

- the copy, right below, is named "… (VST3)", gets the VST3 with default settings, and plays;
- the original keeps the old instrument with all its settings, plus its effects, clips and automation, and is muted and renamed "… (old VST2, muted)".

Everything else on the chain is the same on both tracks, so you only need to copy the instrument's own settings over, then delete the original. You can still pick *Default settings* or *Don't convert* for each plug-in instead. Effects are kept side by side with their VST3 as before.

Every converted set is also checked for duplicate internal IDs before it's saved, so the converter can't produce a set that Live calls corrupt.

**If a conversion made with 0.3.2 or earlier crashes Live**, delete that converted version and convert the original again with 0.3.3.
